svg.text: GM III:9: the philosopher's tendencies "for the longest time went counter to the first demands of morality"
the philosopher's tendencies
doubt · deny · suspend judgment ("ephectic")
analyse · search · explore · dare
compare and equalize
neutrality, objectivity, sine ira et studio
"the incarnate nitimur in vetitum": the forbidden
against
morality and conscience
"the first demands of morality and conscience":
belief, obedience, reverence, not-questioning
so that the philosopher had to guard himself
against his own feelings and instincts
defining instincts that were, for ages, crimes
Daybreak §18's rule, quoted in §9: "all good things were once bad things;
every original sin has become an original virtue"
instances: marriage · gentleness · submission to law, each "introduced by force, as a force,
to which men submitted only with shame"
and the philosopher's tendencies, one more instance
the question this leaves for §10: how did a type whose every instinct was a crime
survive long enough to become a type? §10's answer: by being feared, in the form of a type already feared
